_note: Entries ops/reachability-check.py may not fail on. Read that file's header first: a tombstone is an explicit intentional-not-wired MARK, not a mute button. It must carry a reason and a reopen condition, it must name something still in the tree, and it stops applying — and becomes the finding itself — the moment its entry becomes reachable. Adding one is a decision to be made in the pull request that adds it, in words, not a way to get a red check green.
_seeded: 2026-08-23, from the completion-integrity council's fix D. Every entry below was found by the check's first run against main and is a real gap, not an artefact. None is fixed here on purpose: grok's fix-D procedure is 'mark gaps not-landed, do not remediate mid-sweep', and every one of these remediations is somebody else's call — Joe's for a blocking hook, the fleet's for a service declaration. What the check buys today is the ratchet: no NEW unwired control can enter the tree without an argument for it.

tombstones.reason: Reachable, but only from a surface this check does not read, and that is the finding rather than the file. REGISTRATION_SURFACES is (ops/config/hooks.json, .claude/settings.json), both repo-relative, and claude-tree/ is on the skip list as a retired mirror. The two files claude-tree/ mirrors are NOT gone: ~/My Drive/.claude/settings.json and ~/My Drive/CARR AI/.claude/settings.json each register this hook at SessionStart as `<repo>/.venv/bin/python <repo>/hooks/session-brief.py`, verified by reading both on 2026-08-23 (mtimes Aug 9 and Aug 12). PR #542 reached the same conclusion independently and kept the file for that reason. The earlier reason on this entry said their 'live originals are no longer on this Mac'; that was wrong. What Joe settled on 2026-08-08 still holds — the briefing lives on three surfaces and the universal MCP `instructions` leg carries every client — but the hook leg is running, not dead. THE REAL GAP: those two live settings files are tracked by nothing. config-as-code manages 48 items and none is a vault-rooted settings file, and bin/sync-settings.sh retired the repo mirror without retiring the surface. So a file that fires a hook on every vault-rooted session can drift or be deleted with no producer reporting it. Filed as defect 43febb66 (class: capability-reported-unwired-from-a-surface-nobody-tracks).
tombstones.reopen_when: either the repository gains a tracked declaration of the two vault-rooted SessionStart surfaces — the same relationship ops/config/hooks.json already has to ~/.claude/settings.json, which would let this check see the registration and make the mark unnecessary — or Joe rules that those surfaces are retired for real, at which point the hook leg is deleted along with this entry. Adding the absolute vault paths to REGISTRATION_SURFACES is NOT the fix: it would pass on Joe's Mac and fail in CI, where no vault exists.

tombstones.reason: The council's second named seed. No service in ops/config/services.json declares fleet-sync, so it cannot appear in ops-record health at all: its failure state is not `unknown`, it is unrepresentable. tools/scheduler-truth.py reports the same job from the machine side as INSTALLED, NOT LOADED and SCHEDULED, UNREGISTERED — the plist is in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, launchctl has the label disabled, and nothing has ever fast-forwarded this checkout on a schedule.
tombstones.reopen_when: fleet-sync is declared as a service in ops/config/services.json and bootstrapped, or the plist and bin/fleet-sync.sh are retired together. Declaring it also needs its ops.service row, which is why this is not a one-file edit.

tombstones.reason: Found by this check's first run and independently by tools/scheduler-truth.py, which names it SCHEDULED, UNREGISTERED. Unlike fleet-sync this job is LOADED and running on Joe's Mac right now, which makes it the worse of the two: live work whose health no row can express. tombstones.reason: Superseded rather than unwired, and marked because the supersession was never finished. It merges the record-home gate into ~/.claude/settings.json one hook at a time; ops/config-as-code.py now installs the whole managed block and is the only thing that should write that file. The only references left are records — ops/config/rule-enforcement-map.json, ops/config/gate-baseline.json and the ops.enforcement_control_catalog seed — every one of which still lists it as an installed implementation of the record_home control.
tombstones.reopen_when: it is deleted along with its enforcement-map and catalog references, or it is given a real caller. A completed lifecycle should leave nothing behind pointing at it — rule def3e84e, artifact tombstones: nothing silently rots.
